abstract: Stony corals are foundation species of coral reef ecosystems, yet their biology remains insufficiently explored from an integrative multi-omics perspective. Although the rapid accumulation of genomic and other omics resources offers opportunities to understand coral evolution, development, adaptation, and symbiosis, accessing and utilizing these resources remain challenging. Here, we present CoralDB (http://www.coraldb.net), a comprehensive, genome-centered multi-omics resource that systematically consolidates multi-omics, evolutionary, ecological, and phenotypic data for stony corals and their holobionts. CoralDB covers 414 species and integrates approximately 19 421 datasets, including 12 data dimensions. Moreover, CoralDB offers valuable customized datasets and analytical resources, including standardized functional annotations, gene-family and pan-genome profiles, macro- and microsynteny analyses, spatiotemporal expression patterns, cell-type markers, phylogenetic resources, and symbiont-associated data. An integrated genome browser and interactive modules support flexible data querying, filtering, analysis, visualization, and links to public databases. CoralDB provides an accessible and extensible platform that will help the coral research community manage expanding multi-omics resources, accelerate discoveries in coral biology, evolution, symbiosis, and conservation, and facilitate deeper understanding of reef resilience under accelerating global environmental change.
